title: Dead-code instructions
description: The instructions of the probe of the rules that ask what the change leaves behind: its task, the review, those rules, and the checkout

task.description: What this probe does, said to the probe itself
task.const: Probe the pull request in review against every rule in rulebook.rules and write one row per rule to the file named in review.ledger. These rules ask what the change leaves behind, and finding what it left dead is your task: search the repository at checkout. Outside the surface, report only code this pull request makes dead: a symbol whose last caller it removes, or a branch it makes unreachable. Anchor such a finding at the pull request, name the dead code by file and line in the observation, and name in evidence the surface line that killed it

rulebook.instructions: Apply each rule with its [[term]]s as definitions defines them. When the application of a rule is in doubt, its parent in principles decides

rules.body: Delete [[Test]]s, [[Production code]], and [[Helper code]] that are no longer relevant or used.

principles.parent: Code is a liability, not an asset
principles.body: Always implement things when you actually need them, never when you just foresee that you need them.

definitions.specification: Code that runs a piece of the system and checks that it behaves as specified.
Code that executes in a deployment runtime after the build and serves [[Users]].
Small supporting code that exists to serve other code rather than a user-facing behaviour.
Whoever consumes the software or system to fulfill a need.
